problem:
Given that $x,y\in {C}^{3},$ compute the standard Hermitian inner product $⟨x,y⟩$ of the following two vectors.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-1+i \\ 1 \\ 2-i\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}1+i \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Inner Product in Vector Spaces Over the Complex Numbers

feedback.problem:
Given that $x,y\in {C}^{4},$ compute the standard Hermitian inner product $⟨x,y⟩$ of the following two vectors.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}i \\ -i \\ i \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}i \\ 2 \\ -i \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the definition of the standard Hermitian inner product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}\overset{―}{{y}_{1}}+{x}_{2}\overset{―}{{y}_{2}}+{x}_{3}\overset{―}{{y}_{3}}+{x}_{4}\overset{―}{{y}_{4}} \\  & =i\cdot (\overset{―}{\,i})+(-i)\cdot \overset{―}{2}+i\cdot (\overset{―}{-\text{i}})+(-1)\cdot (\overset{―}{-1}) \\  & =i\cdot (-i)-i\cdot 2+i\cdot \text{i}+(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & =1-2i+(-1)+1 \\  & =1-2i.\end{aligned}
$$
